# CalJab
> CalJab is an iOS food and medicine tracker for people on GLP-1 medicines (such as Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound, Saxenda, Rybelsus and Trulicity), with optional halal and low FODMAP modes. It is available in English, Turkish and Arabic. CalJab is not a medical device; it does not give medical advice and does not suggest doses.

## What it does
- Food logging: photo, one sentence or voice, barcode, search, and picks from a restaurant menu. Daily targets put protein first; for GLP-1 users energy is a lower limit, not a target to hit.
- GLP-1 medicines: dose log with an injection site map and next-site suggestion, dose reminders, missed-dose guidance from official product information, and an estimated medicine level built from leaflet values (an estimate, not a measurement).
- Symptoms: a short daily check-in and a symptom map.
- Supplements and other medicines with reminders. The user enters the amount; the app does not suggest amounts.
- Halal mode leaves out recipes and dishes that are not halal in meal plans and menu picks; a halal note on photo results is an estimate. CalJab does not certify products as halal.
- Low FODMAP mode lets the user mark their step (elimination, reintroduction or personalization), and meal plans and menu picks leave out high FODMAP choices.
- Meal plans, recipes and a shopping list.
- Weight log, and a doctor report (PDF) with doses, weight, symptoms and eating.
- Guide: short articles where every sentence links to its source (see below).
- Ask (Premium): an assistant for short questions about eating, the medicine routine, symptoms and using the app. Answers come from the Guide articles and the user's own records; for dose decisions and for signs of an emergency it shows a fixed card instead of an answer.

## Free and Premium
- Free: manual logging, dose tracking and reminders, the symptom map, safety information, plans and the Guide.
- Premium (monthly, yearly or lifetime; current prices are shown in the App Store): Ask (up to 30 questions a day), unlimited meal photos, voice and one-sentence logging, AI lookup for any food, menu scanning, symptom patterns, dose and weight by week, and the doctor report.

## Privacy
- Health data is used only with the user's consent, asked at sign-up. Withdrawing it in the app deletes health and food logs and meal photos; a download is offered first.
- Data is stored with Supabase in the EU (Frankfurt).
- AI logging receives only the photo or the sentence, not the user's name, modes, medicines, doses or weight.
- Ask has its own consent. With each question it sends the parts of the user's records they leave on (such as medicine, dose and stage, modes, goals, today's meals and symptom days), never their name, email, age, sex, photos or Apple Health data. Chats stay on the phone.
- For adults 18 and over.

## Technical
- Swift and SwiftUI, iOS 17 and later
- Supabase (EU) for accounts and data
- OpenAI models for AI logging and Ask
- StoreKit 2 for subscriptions

## Guide
Short, sourced reads by the CalJab team; every sentence links to its source (medicine leaflets, official health guidance, peer-reviewed papers). Also in Turkish (https://caljab.app/tr/rehber/) and Arabic (https://caljab.app/ar/guide/).
- Index: https://caljab.app/guide/
- [What to expect in the first month](https://caljab.app/guide/first-month/): How the medicine works, why the dose starts low, what can happen in the first weeks, and how to plan your injection day.
- [Storing your pen and travelling](https://caljab.app/guide/pen-storage/): How to store Wegovy and Mounjaro before and after first use, when a pen shouldn't be used, and what to plan when you travel.
- [Smaller portions](https://caljab.app/guide/small-portions/): Why you fill up sooner, how to set up your meals, and what helps while you eat.
- [Fluids and electrolytes](https://caljab.app/guide/hydration/): Why they matter, how much to drink, what counts, and what to do if you are sick or have diarrhea.
- [Nausea and vomiting](https://caljab.app/guide/nausea/): Why it happens, what may help, what to do if you are sick, and when to see a doctor.
- [Constipation and diarrhea](https://caljab.app/guide/constipation-diarrhea/): What may help with constipation and diarrhea, where fiber comes from in FODMAP mode, and when to see a doctor.
- [Reflux and bloating](https://caljab.app/guide/reflux-bloating/): What may help with heartburn, reflux, gas and bloating, and when to see a doctor.
- [When to see a doctor](https://caljab.app/guide/when-to-see-doctor/): Which signs need emergency help, which need a doctor the same day, and which you should tell your doctor about.
- [Contraception, pregnancy and breastfeeding](https://caljab.app/guide/pregnancy-contraception/): How long before a pregnancy to stop, what to know if you take the pill, and what to do if you are breastfeeding.
- [Before surgery or anaesthesia](https://caljab.app/guide/surgery-anaesthesia/): Why to tell your team ahead, whether the medicine is stopped, who is at higher risk, and what your team may ask.
- [Protein when your appetite is low](https://caljab.app/guide/protein-low-appetite/): Why protein matters, how much you need, where to get it when you eat less, and what else protects muscle.
- [Getting enough fiber](https://caljab.app/guide/fiber/): Why fiber matters, how much to aim for, how to add it without upsetting your stomach, and where it comes from in FODMAP mode.
- [Vitamins and minerals when you eat less](https://caljab.app/guide/vitamins-minerals/): Why eating much less can leave gaps, which nutrients to watch, where to find them, and when a supplement or a check-up makes sense.
- [Eating out and at gatherings](https://caljab.app/guide/eating-out/): How to choose at a restaurant, what helps at the table, and what to do at weddings, buffets and parties.
- [Alcohol and GLP-1 medicines](https://caljab.app/guide/alcohol/): Why alcohol can make side effects worse, how to keep the risk low if you drink, and which signs need a doctor.
- [The three steps of FODMAP](https://caljab.app/guide/fodmap-three-steps/): What elimination, reintroduction and personalization mean, how long they take, and what to know before you start.
- [Eating out on a low FODMAP diet](https://caljab.app/guide/fodmap-eating-out/): How to plan ahead, what to order and what to ask the kitchen so you can eat out on a low FODMAP diet.
- [Reading labels](https://caljab.app/guide/label-reading/): How to read an ingredients list, how to check halal certification, and how to spot FODMAP ingredients.
- [Fasting in Ramadan on a GLP-1 medicine](https://caljab.app/guide/ramadan/): When to talk to your doctor, whether the injection breaks the fast, your dose, suhoor and iftar, and when to break the fast.
- [Protecting your muscle](https://caljab.app/guide/muscle/): Why some muscle can go while you lose weight, who is at higher risk, and how strength training and protein help.
- [When weight loss slows down](https://caljab.app/guide/plateau/): Why weight loss slows over time, why a plateau is not a reason to stop, and what can help.
- [Habits that help keep weight off](https://caljab.app/guide/maintenance-habits/): What people who keep weight off tend to do, and why it helps to build these habits while you're on the medicine.
- [If you stop the medicine](https://caljab.app/guide/stopping/): What studies show happens to weight after stopping, why to plan it with your doctor, and the habits that matter.
